routes.description: Establish robust non-naturalist normative realism by treating objective normative facts as legitimate explananda, defending normative appearances as justified starting points, and showing that realism best preserves ordinary judgment, deliberation, and language under holistic comparison.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if objective normative facts remain warranted components of inquiry, challenges from intuition diversity and causal genealogy do not defeat that warrant, and rival pragmatist or attitude-based accounts fail to explain the relevant normative phenomena without comparable commitments.

motionBridge.description: Connect justified mind-independent normative facts, including moral facts, to the motion's claim that objective moral truths exist and favor realism over global normative anti-realism.

centralBridges.description: Show why normative facts themselves, rather than only beliefs, behavior, or linguistic practices, are legitimate phenomena requiring explanation.
Explain why plausible normative appearances can justify inquiry without prior proof and why unshared intuitions do not establish epistemic parity.
Demonstrate through holistic comparison that realism preserves normative judgment and deliberation with lower theoretical costs than its rivals.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish genuine causal debunking evidence from cultural variation, minority status, disagreement, or the mere absence of explicit folk metaethical views.
Require attitude-based semantics and quietism to account for counterfactual moral claims, ordinary linguistic practice, and the apparent intelligibility of metaethical questions.

routes.description: Establish global normative anti-realism by denying realism any privileged intuitive or explanatory starting point and providing pragmatist, psychological, and meaning-in-use accounts of moral judgment, language, deliberation, and opposition without objective non-naturalist facts.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if realist appearances can be explained without truth-tracking access, ordinary moral practice carries no necessary realist commitment, and objective normative facts add no explanatory work beyond a more parsimonious descriptive account.

motionBridge.description: Connect the absence of a warranted or explanatorily necessary objective normative posit to global normative anti-realism and rejection of objective moral truths.

centralBridges.description: Show that realist intuitions and normative appearances are neither universal nor entitled to methodological priority over anti-realist starting points.
Explain moral psychology, deliberation, behavior, and discourse through attitudes, communicative intentions, social practices, and empirical causal accounts.
Establish that realism supplies no indispensable explanation and that a pragmatist framework can dissolve or bypass its proposed metaphysical problem.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify an error-producing causal history or methodological mechanism capable of explaining localized realist belief without tracking objective normative truth.
Account for sincere condemnation, counterfactual opposition, and action-guiding moral speech without committing speakers or sentences to mind-independent moral facts.

sections.title: Scope, Explananda, and Comparative Burdens
sections.rationale: The debate first turns on whether the target is morality or normativity generally, whether normative facts themselves belong among the data, and how competing theoretical packages should be compared.

sections.title: Normative Appearances and Epistemic Priority
sections.rationale: The central epistemic clash concerns whether realist appearances may function as justified starting points, whether contrary intuitions create parity, and whether disagreement without persuasion affects warrant.

sections.title: Moral Judgment, Language, and Deliberation
sections.rationale: Both routes must explain objective-seeming judgments, counterfactual wrongness, sincere condemnation, linguistic meaning, and action-guiding deliberation while establishing whether those practices carry realist commitments.

sections.title: Empirical Genealogy, Variation, and Debunking
sections.rationale: Cultural variation, folk research, minority status, shared philosophical methods, and causal error hypotheses matter insofar as they distinguish harmless diversity from a genuine debunking explanation.

sections.title: Explanatory Necessity, Parsimony, and Quietism
sections.rationale: The culminating comparative issue is whether objective normative facts perform indispensable explanatory work or whether pragmatist and descriptive accounts explain moral practice more parsimoniously and challenge the framing itself.
